svg.title: Persistence as a chain of contracts
svg.desc: Applications request named updates, the VFS and filesystem manipulate objects and cached state, the block layer and device persist ordered writes, and recovery reconstructs a valid namespace after failure.
svg.text: Persistence is a chain of contracts, not a property of write() alone
Application
create, rename, append, replace, delete
declares when visibility and durability matter
named intent
VFS + namespace
resolve path components, mount crossings and permissions
bind names to objects and open handles
naming + sharing
Filesystem
update inodes, directories, extents, free-space state and log
maintain invariants across several dependent blocks
structure + ordering
Cache + I/O stack
delay, batch, schedule, flush and report writeback errors
translate logical blocks into device requests
transport
Storage + recovery
retain acknowledged writes across the stated failure model
replay, roll back or reconcile after restart
durability + recovery
errors and recovered state flow upward
system-call boundary
A correct application must know which layer has acknowledged visibility, ordering and durable completion.
